evaluation: bemlops time-ordered split with 1-h gaps over the valid 15-min intervals (train 2021-09-07..11-05, validation 11-05..11-12, test 11-12..12-09). The chosen random forest scored test RMSE 0.72 kWh (MAE 0.36 kWh, CV(RMSE) 21.9%, NMBE +4.1%, Guideline 14 hourly passes) against 2.55 kWh for persistence, a skill of 0.72. Two forward folds of my own agreed: 0.69 kWh testing from 11-08, and 1.0 kWh testing 10-26..11-05 with only 9 training days and a public holiday. The deployed model is the same configuration refit on all valid data; I add about 0.1 kWh for the unseen season and semester break, holidays and new meter faults.
data_findings: Format: 5-min rows, timestamps with +08:00, kept as naive Singapore local time. Weekdays only: no Saturday or Sunday rows at all, so the model has never seen a weekend. Gaps: 2021-10-02..10-24, 11-18..12-08, 09-23 14:00..09-24 02:00, 10-28 21:00..23:25.
288 rows of 2021-11-15/16 were exported twice (identical values): duplicates dropped. A block of 29 rows on 2021-10-28 evening is in reverse time order: sorted.
17 target readings are -999 placeholders, and outdoor RH has 14 'OFFLINE' text entries: both set to missing.

air_temperature switches from degC to degF at 2021-11-08 04:45 (values 79-86) and stays in degF to the end. Converted row by row: any reading above 55 is treated as degF. The same guard is applied to the other temperature points in case they switch later.
Outdoor dry-bulb has 8 single-sample spikes of 41-51 degC (impossible in Singapore) and VOC has one spike of 3922 ppb: set to missing with fixed row-wise limits.

The biggest problem is the target. The chilled-water meter reads exactly 0 from 2021-09-21 to 2021-10-26 10:25 (10 of the 37 operating days in the export plus a morning; 1,472 5-min readings masked in total with the faults below) while the AHU fan runs at ~29 Hz with the CHW valve 45-50% open, so this is a meter fault, not zero load. It also has short dropouts followed by catch-up dumps: on 09-13 it reads zeros from 16:40 to 17:20 and then 14.4 kWh in one 5-min sample (normal is ~2), on 11-17 several more, then 0 from 15:35 to shutdown. From 11-03 18:40 to 11-04 10:00 it is stuck at 0.4846 kWh per 5 min while the AHU is off. All of these are masked using same-time readings only (target 0 while fan > 5 Hz and valve command > 5%; target > 0 while the fan is off now and 5 min earlier; any 5-min value above 6 kWh). They are left missing, never filled, in training and in the lagged inputs at forecast time.
Target definition: 15-min energy is the sum of the three 5-min readings, and is missing unless all three are valid. After masking, 2,984 valid 15-min targets remain out of 3,504 intervals with data.

Operation: the AHU runs 08:05-18:40 every weekday. Chilled-water energy is ~6.5-7 kWh per 15 min while running and 0 otherwise. There is a start-up peak at 08:15 and a regular rise at 18:15-18:30 before shutdown; the 18:15 interval alone accounts for ~17% of the squared error. On the 2021-11-04 public holiday (Deepavali) the AHU ran only 10:05-17:40.

supply_air_flow and damper_position are stuck for days (93.15 for 3 days; 1942.828 and 72.98 overnight) and missing for 2 weeks: not used. offcoil_temp_setpoint is constant: not used. The off-coil and supply-air temperatures repeat one value for ~6 h after weekend gaps (the export holds the last value). This only happens with the AHU off, so it was left as is.
Outdoor RH sits at 99.9-100% for many nights. This is real saturation, not a stuck sensor.

bemlops stuck and spike masking were switched off because they are not causal (see usability). All fault handling above is row-wise or uses earlier rows only. I verified this: truncating the file at 6 cut times and on a synthetic longer, corrupted file gives forecasts identical to the full-file run, bit for bit, for every T <= cut + 45 min.

Features (bemlops-built and audited): target lags 1-1.75 h, 1 day and 1 week; 1-day rolling mean; measured inputs lagged 1 h (fan speed, CHW valve command/position, off-coil and supply air temperatures, zone temperature/RH/CO2, occupant count, wifi devices, outdoor temperature/RH, solar, AHU fan, lighting and plug energy); hour/day-of-week calendar. My additions: known-ahead time of day, an 08:00-18:45 schedule window and a Singapore public-holiday flag; and a measured feature (lagged by bemlops), the mean chilled-water energy over the last 39 valid in-schedule intervals, which skips weekends and gaps. Model: bemlops random forest (150 trees, max_depth 16, max_features 0.3), chosen over gradient boosting on validation (0.63 vs 0.65 kWh), then refit on all valid rows.
usability: prepare() stuck and spike masking are not causal, and the docs do not say so. A stretch counts as 'stuck' only after it has lasted stuck_hours, and a single-sample spike needs the next sample, so whether a reading is masked depends on later data. Verified: with data cut at 2021-11-03 23:00, 52 target readings from 18:40 to 22:55 stay unmasked; with the later data present they are masked. ForecastModel.predict re-runs prepare() on live data, so live forecasts and backtests on a growing file change after the fact. That contradicts 'nothing comes from the future'. I had to turn off mask_stuck and mask_spikes and handle faults row-wise myself. Please make these causal in live mode, or warn about it.

With mask_stuck/mask_spikes off, check_data() and the saved report.md still say 'prepare() treats these stretches as missing' for each stuck/spike warning. The run record describes cleaning that did not happen.

ForecastModel.predict(future=True) appends the next horizon rows, but known_ahead inputs are NaN there and get silently imputed with the training median. My first version produced wrong forecasts for the last hour of every file: up to 6.3 kWh off, found only by a truncation test. predict should warn or raise, or take the known-ahead values for the future rows. I now append the future rows with calendar values myself and call predict(future=False).

Known-ahead columns are forward-filled like measured ones (prepare_log shows forward_fill for tod_min, sched_window and holiday). Forward-filling a calendar or schedule column is wrong. They should be required for every row, or computed.

fit() keeps the estimator trained on train+validation only: train_end is 2021-11-12, so the most recent ~6 operating days, the ones closest to deployment, are never used. There is no option to refit the chosen configuration on all data. retrain() does champion/challenger and does not cover this. I cloned model.estimator and refit it on features.build_features(...) with the saved target_lags, after checking that the rebuilt features reproduce the saved model's predictions exactly.

fit() with defaults took ~32 min for ~3,000 rows on a busy 8-core machine, with no progress output. Project.fit, check_data and DataReport have no docstrings, and the default n_iter and the time cost are not documented. models=['random_forest','gbm'] with n_iter=12 took 2.4 min.

The saved random-forest pipeline has n_jobs=-1. Its multi-threaded prediction adds tree outputs in a varying order, so repeated forecasts from the same data differ by ~1e-15. That breaks exact-equality reproducibility and leakage checks. I set model__n_jobs=1 at load time.

No cross-sensor plausibility check. The chilled-water meter read 0 for 10 operating days (2021-09-21 to 10-26) while the AHU fan ran and the CHW valve was 45-50% open, and check_data reported nothing: energy zeros are never flagged as stuck. Neither is the dropout-then-catch-up pattern (zeros, then one sample worth the missed energy). This is a common BAS meter fault, and it was the single biggest data problem here.

The mid-series unit switch (zone temperature degC -> degF on 2021-11-08) is reported as out_of_range for 26% of readings with the advice 'check the declaration'. That steers you toward changing the whole column's unit. Saying 'values change unit at <timestamp>' would be more useful.
False positive: outdoor RH holding at 99.9-100% for 15-17 h at night (normal tropical saturation) is flagged as stuck and would be masked by default. RH near 100% should not count as stuck.

Missing quantities and units: no hPa for pressure, no VOC, sound level or water flow, no occupant-proxy count (wifi devices). These all had to be 'other'. There is no holiday calendar (I hard-coded Singapore holidays). The is_weekend feature is kept even though it is constant (0) in the training data.

The 'forecast_made_at' column in predict output is T - 1 h, but the forecast uses the 15-min bin [T-1h, T-45min), i.e. data up to T - 45 min. The label is the bin start, which is confusing when you audit leakage.
Minor: SKILL.md says 'pip install bemlops', but README says it is not on PyPI.
